description: Release test matrix: every configuration Opfield supports, with the scenario that proves it before a stable tag. Built from what the installers parse and the docs promise, not from changelogs. scripts/release-matrix.test.mjs keeps it complete. Stand scenarios run on a stand before every stable tag; static scenarios run in CI. Steps are stand-agnostic; the stand runbook maps them to hosts.

conventions.covers: '<installer> <option>' or '<installer> <option>=<value>'; '<installer> $<VARIABLE>' or '<installer> $<VARIABLE>=<value>'; 'config <key>' (a daemon config key documented in docs/nodes.md); 'feature <id>' (declared under features); 'lifecycle <daemon> <operation>' (declared under lifecycle).

placeholders.<setup command>: The command Nodes > Add Node shows for the node type (the same as installCommands from POST /api/nodes), with the release, Opfield address, token and certificate fingerprint it generated.
placeholders.<opfield>, <token>, <cert>: The Opfield gRPC address, enrollment token and gRPC certificate fingerprint of a node created in Opfield.
placeholders.<candidate>: The release under test, for example v2.11.1.
placeholders.<previous>: The latest stable release before the candidate of the same major line.
placeholders.<newer>: A release of the same line newer than the candidate, published on the preview channel.
placeholders.gwsvc, gwsvc2, gwdock, gwdock2: System users created for the run: useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin <name> (Alpine: adduser -S -D -H -s /sbin/nologin <name>).
placeholders.connected: The installer prints '<daemon> is connected to Opfield' (the relay: that the supervisor enrolled and connected) and exits 0; the node is online in GET /api/nodes with daemonVersion equal to the installed release.
placeholders.service user: systemd: systemctl show -p User,Group <unit>; OpenRC: rc-service <unit> status and ps -o user= -p <daemon pid>.

os.debian: Debian 13 with systemd. The main target: every scenario runs here unless it is specific to another system.
os.alpine: Alpine Linux 3.x with OpenRC. Installer and service-manager behaviour.
os.alpine-noinit: An Alpine Linux 3.x container without an init system or service manager, where the installers use manual mode.
os.ubuntu: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with systemd, AppArmor and systemd-resolved. Only where it differs from Debian: packaged nginx 1.24, the distribution docker.io, AppArmor and the resolved stub DNS. In an LXC guest the host confines the guest, so AppArmor coverage there is partial; a VM gives the full picture.

installer.generated-command.description: The setup command of Nodes > Add Node downloads the installer from this Opfield's release, runs it only after the release checksum matches, pins --version to the newest daemon release of the same minor, and appends --disable-console/--disable-files when their checkboxes are set.

installer.universal-command.description: setup-daemon.sh downloads the installer for --type from the same release, verifies it against the release checksums and forwards every other argument.

installer.release-mirror.description: Installers fetch release metadata, daemon artifacts and sibling installers from overridden locations and refuse a file whose checksum does not match.

installer.interactive.description: Without -y the installers prompt only for missing values and the storage installer offers its disk selector.

installer.connection-check.description: An install or re-run succeeds only when the started daemon runs under the service manager and Opfield accepted its session; otherwise it exits 1 naming the daemon log and printing its last lines.

installer.legacy-daemon-check.description: A daemon release older than the session signal is accepted after its service stayed active for 10 seconds, with a warning that it does not report its Opfield connection.

installer.manual-mode.description: On a host without systemd or OpenRC the installers start a detached launcher that does not survive a reboot, and still wait for the Opfield session.

installer.dry-run.description: --dry-run validates the inputs and prints the real plan without changing the host.

installer.apt-lock-retry.description: The nginx installer retries apt while another process holds the dpkg lock.

node.console-as-user.description: The node console runs as the daemon's user, or, on a root daemon, as console.user when it is set (in / when that user has no home); a non-root daemon refuses another console.user with the reason.

node.files-as-user.description: Node file operations run with the daemon user's permissions and a refused path fails at once with permission denied.

node.wrapper.description: A non-root daemon runs from /usr/local/lib/<daemon>/bin; /usr/local/bin/<daemon> is a root-owned wrapper that switches a root caller to the service user.

node.host-identity.description: All daemons of a host report one host identity; a non-root daemon reads its copy through host_identity_path while the shared file stays root-only.

node.host-access-switches.description: console.enabled/files.enabled false refuse the host console and host files with 409, survive installer re-runs and are turned back on only in the config file.

node.manual-setup.description: A daemon installed by hand from the release files, enrolled with '<daemon> install' and run by a hand-written service.

node.update-bulk.description: Update from the node page and Nodes > Update Nodes for several nodes at once.

node.update-refusals.description: Opfield refuses a daemon update for a disconnected node, a relay node and a node already on that release, and records the reason of a failed update.

node.update-lease-peers.description: Nodes that share a lease-mode Availability policy update one after another (waiting_for_lease_peers).

node.update-from-previous.description: Daemons of the previous stable release update to the candidate through Opfield.

node.launcher-rollback.description: The launcher keeps the previous binary and rolls a candidate back that does not stay ready through its stability window.

node.launcher-self-update.description: A launcher updates itself in place to the launcher of a committed daemon and keeps its process, its daemon and the sockets it holds; a launcher process that predates this takes the next daemon update as one restart of the whole service.

node.service-address.description: An explicit Docker service address on the node page is the endpoint of managed database links and published storage; proxy routes to Docker workloads go through a Secure Link and do not use it.

nginx.managed.description: managed mode on a fresh host installs nginx (nginx.org stable on Debian and Ubuntu, the distribution package on Alpine) and writes the base config.

nginx.integrate-existing.description: integrate mode keeps the host's nginx config and its own 443 default server, injects the managed includes and a local stub_status.

nginx.tls-catch-all.description: The managed 443 default server refuses TLS for names without a route.

nginx.nonroot.description: nginx-daemon as the user that runs the nginx master: preflight refusals, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for nginx -t, route apply and reload, and the switch back to root.

nginx.nonroot-apparmor.description: A non-root nginx-daemon applies routes, runs nginx -t and reloads with AppArmor loaded (partial in an LXC guest).

nginx.old-version.description: An existing nginx older than 1.25.1: refused non-interactively and with --skip-nginx, upgraded from nginx.org only after interactive approval.

nginx.maintenance.description: Route maintenance without an nginx reload, team access codes, maintenance across daemon restart and host reboot.

nginx.acme-pages-logs.description: ACME HTTP-01 files, Pages deploys, live route logs and the ingress health endpoint on an nginx node.

nginx.ingress-groups.description: Ingress groups: members render every route, an offline member catches up on reconnect, removal drains.

docker.engine-install.description: The Docker installer installs Docker Engine on a host without it (docker-ce from docker.com on Debian, the docker package on Alpine) and writes json-file log rotation defaults.

docker.existing-engine.description: An existing distribution Docker Engine (docker.io) and its daemon.json are kept; Secure Runtime only adds runtimes.runsc to daemon.json, after a backup.

docker.old-engine.description: Workloads on Docker Engine 20.10 to 25.x (Debian 12 docker.io is 20.10): recreate, migration preflight and migration to a current engine.

docker.nonroot.description: docker-daemon as a member of the docker group: socket preflight, connectors through the daemon's group, reported root-only features.

docker.nonroot-apparmor.description: Root and non-root docker-daemon, its connector containers and workloads with AppArmor loaded (partial in an LXC guest).

docker.connector-mode-switch.description: Secure Links and storage links keep working across root and non-root switches without a manual step.

docker.secure-runtime.description: Secure Runtime (gVisor): preflight and install on a fresh install, --secure-runtime on an existing root or non-root node, the runtime CLI exit codes, Secure workloads and their boundaries.

docker.secure-runtime-apparmor.description: --secure-runtime with AppArmor loaded, root and non-root: Secure Runtime installs where gVisor can run, otherwise the installer fails with the preflight reason (partial in an LXC guest).

docker.lease-watchdog.description: The lease watchdog is installed as its own root service in docker mode, reports with 'opfield-lease-watchdog status', and OPFIELD_LEASE_WATCHDOG_VERSION pins its release.

docker.watchdog-auto-install.description: A 2.11 docker-daemon running as root installs the lease watchdog by itself on a node installed before it existed.

docker.container-lifecycle.description: Stop, restart, kill and delete of containers, including ones that ignore SIGTERM, through REST, MCP and UI.

docker.migration.description: Cross-node migration of containers and deployments with a route: preflight, maintenance flag during cutover, completion.

docker.compose.description: Compose Projects: apply recreates only changed services, the first apply after the daemon update recreates once.

docker.archives.description: .gwca export and import in portable and registry-backed mode.

docker.log-limits.description: Containers Opfield creates get json-file rotation only while the host default allows it.

docker.gpu.description: Attaching a discovered physical GPU to a container and a deployment.

docker.dns-resolved.description: Containers and connectors resolve names on a host whose resolv.conf is the systemd-resolved stub.

builder.egress.description: Build Worker egress internet (public downloads, private and control-plane ranges and the worker host itself blocked) and offline.

builder.egress-dns-resolved.description: A Build Worker with egress internet resolves dependency hosts on a systemd-resolved host.

builder.order.description: Queued builds go to Build Workers in the order of the Nodes list, folders first.

builder.requires-systemd.description: The builder profile refuses a host without systemd before changing it.

storage.loop-preflight.description: The Storage installer proves the loop and ext4 lifecycle before enrollment and refuses an ordinary LXC guest without changing it.

storage.root-selector.description: The interactive disk selector and --storage-root choose the storage root.

storage.legacy-databases.description: A node installed with the legacy databases alias keeps its identity and storage root and gets the Storage capabilities after a daemon update.

storage.managed-databases.description: Managed PostgreSQL, Redis and ClickHouse: TCP publication and ports, supervisor restarts, retry of failed provisioning, lost-record recovery.

storage.managed-object-storage.description: Managed SeaweedFS: engine supervision, retry and record recovery, storage links.

storage.backups-copy-jobs.description: Database backup policies, runs, restores, retention and storage copy jobs on Storage executors.

relay.pool-membership.description: A relay node enrolls, is ready in the Relay Pool and carries Secure Link traffic.

relay.low-port.description: A non-root relay on a port below 1024 gets CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE; 9443 and root get none.

relay.reenroll.description: Re-enroll from Settings > Relay with a single-use token; a refused token keeps the previous identity.

relay.certificate-renewal.description: Remote relay certificates renew on their own and with Renew certificate.

relay.pool-update.description: Relay Pool update: supervisor first, then worker, one relay at a time, resumable.

relay.rebalance-drain.description: Rebalance, drain with the 30 minute wait and Force disconnect.

availability.replicated.description: Availability in Replicated mode: enable, stop, start, rollout, disable with a route.

availability.failover-lease.description: Failover policies in lease mode: entering lease mode, autonomous failover with and without Opfield, planned handoff, priority failback, excluded nodes.

availability.nonroot-watchdog.description: A non-root Docker node takes part in lease mode through the root watchdog service the installer sets up.

opfield.install.description: install.sh fresh install with the default native HTTPS, setup code and wizard, and its re-run as an update.

opfield.install-variants.description: install.sh with HTTP, the interactive transport prompt, another install directory, a resumed interrupted install and the host Docker logging defaults.

opfield.install-from-source.description: install.sh --source-dir builds a fresh test installation from a checkout and refuses an existing one.

opfield.update-in-app.description: In-app Opfield update: waiting for running operations, Update now, database snapshot, the update channel.

opfield.update-from-2.10.description: The upgrade path from the 2.10 line including the base updater's rollback.

opfield.web-transport.description: Switching internal HTTPS on and off in Settings.

opfield.offline.description: With the Opfield app down, nginx keeps serving with the cached status page, containers run, daemons reconnect afterwards.

hosting.adoption.description: Automatic adoption of a Proxmox guest whose node runs a non-root daemon, by host identity.

hosting.create-node.description: Creating a hosted node on Proxmox: provisioning, installation, enrollment, readiness and Retry installation.

dashboard.attention.description: The sidebar Dashboard dot and the Dashboard warnings show the same conditions.

operations.fresh-root: First install on a host without this daemon, as root: connected, service user root.
operations.fresh-user: First install with a non-root service user: connected, service user is that user.
operations.rerun: Re-run on an enrolled, online node with the same user and no token: connected, no new enrollment, launcher kept.
operations.root-to-user: Re-run of a root install with --user: the daemon's directories go to the user, no new enrollment, same host identity.
operations.user-to-root: Re-run of a non-root install without --user: root gets back only what the previous user owned, the wrapper becomes a root binary.
operations.user-to-user: Re-run of a non-root install with another user.
operations.refused-user: A user that does not exist, or a non-root user for a root-only profile: exit 1 before any host change.
operations.token-refused: An already used or expired token: exit 1 at once with 'Opfield refused the enrollment token', without the reachability hint.
operations.opfield-unreachable: Opfield cannot be reached: exit 1 after the enrollment wait with the daemon log source and its last lines.
operations.prerequisites: A missing or unsupported prerequisite (packages, nginx version or user, Docker socket, loop devices, service manager) is installed or refused before any change, as documented.
operations.service-fails: The service of an enrolled node cannot start: the re-run exits 1 with the log tail and no manual-mode fallback.
operations.restart: A service-manager restart: online again, no restart loop.
operations.reboot: A host reboot: online again with the same service user.
operations.self-update: Opfield updates the daemon to a newer release: new version, previous binary kept, owner and service user unchanged.
operations.dry-run: --dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing.

notApplicable.fresh-user: The builder profile runs only as root; a non-root user is refused-user.
notApplicable.token-refused: The same setup-docker-node.sh enrollment and session check as the docker profile.
notApplicable.opfield-unreachable: The same setup-docker-node.sh session wait as the docker profile.
notApplicable.service-fails: The same setup-docker-node.sh service start and check as the docker profile.

notApplicable.fresh-user: Storage nodes run only as root; a non-root user is refused-user.
notApplicable.token-refused: setup-database-node.sh hands enrollment to setup-docker-node.sh, the same check as the docker profile.
notApplicable.opfield-unreachable: The same setup-docker-node.sh session wait as the docker profile.
notApplicable.service-fails: The same setup-docker-node.sh service start and check as the docker profile.

scenarios.title: Every installer parses, dry-runs each profile and takes its settings from options and the environment
preconditions: Linux CI runner; the test copies the installers, points their host paths at an empty directory and stubs docker, nginx and curl.
steps: bash -n and the define-before-use check on every setup-*.sh.
--dry-run of each installer and profile, as root and with --user, with and without --disable-console --disable-files.
The same dry runs with every setting from the OPFIELD_* environment instead of options, and with --host/--port/--no-logo.
Invalid values through the environment (--mode, --builder-egress, --nginx-mode, --secure-runtime outside docker, a non-root database node, a missing relay user or group).
setup-daemon.sh --type <each type> with --script-dir and with OPFIELD_SETUP_SCRIPT_DIR, and an unknown type.
--help of every installer and install.sh.
expect: Every dry run exits 0, prints 'console.enabled: false'/'files.enabled: false' for the switches, the storage root given by --storage-root or OPFIELD_DATABASE_STORAGE_ROOT, 'integrate mode' for OPFIELD_NODE_NGINX_MODE, the Build Worker profile for OPFIELD_DOCKER_MODE=builder, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for a non-root relay on port 853, and no 'command not found'.
Every invalid value exits non-zero with the installer's own message.
setup-daemon.sh runs the local installer of each type; an unknown type exits non-zero.
Every --help exits 0 with a Usage line.

scenarios.title: Launcher rollback, session file and host access refusals in the daemon test suite
preconditions: CI runs the Go tests as a non-root user.
steps: pnpm test:light:go runs shared/lifecycle (launcher, candidate directories, rollback, launcher update in place and service restart, control-session.json), the lease watchdog and the host access refusal tests.
expect: All packages pass; a candidate that does not stay ready is rolled back to the preserved binary.

A launcher with a daemon and a kept listener execs into the staged launcher with the same PID, the daemon and the listener survive; an update under a launcher without self-update plans one service restart under systemd and OpenRC and none in manual mode; under OpenRC so does an update under a launcher with launcher_self_update_v1 but without launcher_openrc_v1 (2.11.4-rc.6); OpenRC's supervise-daemon is recognized although its comm reads supervise-daemo.

scenarios.title: The generated setup command and the universal setup-daemon.sh command
preconditions: A host prepared for node installs (bash, curl and sudo present).
Opfield runs <candidate>.
steps: Create a monitoring node in Nodes > Add Node with both Disable host console/files checkboxes set; copy the command.

Check the command: it downloads from the <candidate> release, checks sha256sum against opfield-node-installers.sha256 and passes --version with the newest daemon release of the <candidate> minor, plus --disable-console --disable-files.
Run it as given.

On Debian also run the universal form: curl -sSL <release>/download/<candidate>/setup-daemon.sh | sudo bash -s -- --type monitoring --version <candidate> --opfield <opfield> --token <token> --opfield-cert-sha256 <cert> -y on a second token, and once with OPFIELD_SETUP_VERSION=<candidate> instead of --version.
expect: connected; console.enabled: false and files.enabled: false in /etc/monitoring-daemon/config.yaml; GET /api/nodes shows nodeConsoleDisabled and nodeFilesDisabled true.
setup-daemon.sh logs 'Downloading verified setup-monitoring-node.sh' from download/<candidate> and the installer it ran is byte-identical to the release asset.
A tampered checksum file (served through OPFIELD_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE in INS-GEN-02) is refused; here the published one passes.

scenarios.title: Release locations overridden through the environment, and checksum refusal
preconditions: A local HTTP server on the tool host mirrors the <candidate> GitHub release assets, the release feed answer for each component and the daemon artifact directories, with an access log.
A host where monitoring-daemon and the relay are not installed yet.
steps: Without --version, run --dry-run of setup-node.sh, setup-docker-node.sh, setup-monitoring-node.sh and setup-relay-node.sh with OPFIELD_RELEASES_API_URL and OPFIELD_ARTIFACT_BASE_URL pointing at the mirror.
Replace the monitoring-daemon binary on the mirror with a modified copy and run the monitoring installer with the same variables; restore the binary.
Install the relay of INS-RLY-01 for real with the same variables and no --version.
Run setup-daemon.sh --type storage --dry-run and the piped setup-storage-node.sh (no sibling files) --dry-run with OPFIELD_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE=<mirror> and OPFIELD_SETUP_VERSION=<candidate>.
Replace setup-database-node.sh on the mirror with a modified copy and repeat the storage dry run.
expect: The dry runs resolve <candidate> from the mirror (its access log shows the feed requests) and exit 0.
The modified daemon binary fails checksum verification with exit 1; /usr/local/bin/monitoring-daemon does not exist and no service was created.
The relay downloads only from the mirror and is ready.
The storage dry runs fetch setup-database-node.sh and setup-docker-node.sh from <mirror>/download/<candidate>/ and exit 0.
The modified installer stops with 'Checksum verification failed for setup-database-node.sh' and exit 1.

scenarios.title: Interactive installs prompt only for missing values
preconditions: A terminal session (tmux) on a host without docker-daemon; a fresh docker token. INS-DKR-03 can use this install.
steps: sudo bash setup-docker-node.sh --opfield <opfield> --user gwdock (no -y, no token, no fingerprint).
Answer the token and fingerprint prompts.
Re-run with only --user gwdock on the enrolled node with OPFIELD_SETUP_NO_CLEAR=1.
expect: Only the token and fingerprint are asked; Docker version and the plan are shown; connected.
The re-run says 'Existing enrolled docker node detected — reusing the current Opfield connection settings', asks nothing, does not clear the terminal and is connected.

scenarios.title: nginx install while apt is locked
preconditions: A host without nginx, before INS-NGX-01.
steps: Hold the dpkg frontend lock the way apt does, for 20 s: python3 -c 'import fcntl,time; f=open("/var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend","w"); fcntl.lockf(f,fcntl.LOCK_EX); time.sleep(20)' &
While it is held, run the nginx setup command with OPFIELD_NODE_APT_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=2 OPFIELD_NODE_APT_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=2.
Hold the lock again and run INS-NGX-01 with OPFIELD_NODE_APT_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=12 OPFIELD_NODE_APT_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=5.
expect: With 2 attempts the installer prints 'Package manager is busy; retrying in 2s (1/2)' and then fails with the apt error, before changing nginx config or enrolling.
With 12 attempts it retries until the lock is released and the install completes.

scenarios.title: Manual mode on a host without a service manager
preconditions: Throwaway Alpine containers with bash, curl and sudo and no init: one with host networking for monitoring and relay, one with nginx installed from apk, one docker:dind container for the docker profile.
Fresh tokens for a monitoring, relay, nginx and docker node.
steps: In each container run the setup command with OPFIELD_MANUAL_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60 (monitoring also once with --user gwsvc; relay with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc and a port above 1024; nginx with --nginx-mode integrate after starting nginx).
Re-run the monitoring installer on the enrolled container.
Stop the container and start it again.
expect: Each installer prints '<daemon> is running in manual mode (launcher PID …)', 'Manual mode is not persistent across reboot', then connected; manual.log is owned by the service user.
The re-run stops the previous launcher (its cmdline matched) and starts one new launcher; exactly one launcher runs afterwards.
After the container restart the daemon does not run, as documented; re-running the installer brings it back.

scenarios.title: Missing prerequisites are installed or refused before any change
preconditions: monitoring-daemon and the relay are not installed on the host; nginx from the distribution and Docker Engine run as root (a root nginx-daemon or docker-daemon may already be enrolled).
steps: Download setup-monitoring-node.sh and setup-relay-node.sh, then remove curl and jq with the package manager.
Run the monitoring installer from the file with --user gwsvc; run the relay installer from the file with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc.
Make the Docker socket unusable for its group (chgrp root on the socket; Docker recreates it on restart), run setup-docker-node.sh --user gwdock, then restart Docker.
Run setup-node.sh --user www-data --nginx-mode integrate (Alpine: --user nginx) while nginx still runs as root.
Run setup-node.sh --user www-data --nginx-mode managed after preparing nginx as in INS-NGX-02.
expect: The monitoring installer installs curl and ca-certificates (apt or apk) and is connected; the relay installer installs jq and is connected.

The Docker installer adds gwdock to the docker group, then stops with "User 'gwdock' cannot use the Docker socket" and exit 1; an existing docker-daemon keeps its configuration, service user and connection.
The nginx installer stops with the list of what to prepare and 'nothing was changed'; an existing nginx-daemon, its configuration and /etc/nginx/opfield are unchanged.
managed mode with a non-root user is refused before any change.

scenarios.title: A refused enrollment token
preconditions: A clean host at the end of its group (the host is reset afterwards); for each of monitoring, nginx and docker a token that already enrolled another node.
steps: Run each setup command with the used token.
expect: Each installer exits 1 within seconds with 'Opfield refused the enrollment token (already used, expired, or for another node): … Create a new setup command', names the daemon log and prints its last lines.
No 'check that Opfield … is reachable' hint is printed.

scenarios.title: Opfield unreachable during a re-run
preconditions: Enrolled, online monitoring, nginx, docker and relay daemons on the host.
steps: Add a firewall rule on the host that drops traffic to the Opfield gRPC port.
Re-run each installer with its wait variable set to 30 (OPFIELD_NODE_ENROLLMENT_WAIT_SECONDS, OPFIELD_MONITORING_ENROLLMENT_WAIT_SECONDS, OPFIELD_RELAY_ENROLLMENT_WAIT_SECONDS).
Remove the rule and re-run once more.
expect: Each re-run exits 1 after about 30 s with 'has not connected to Opfield within 30 s; check that Opfield at <opfield> is reachable', 'Daemon log: journalctl -u <unit>' (Alpine: the OpenRC log files) and the last 20 lines.
After the rule is removed each re-run is connected.

scenarios.title: A service that cannot start fails the re-run
preconditions: Enrolled, online monitoring, nginx, docker and relay daemons on the host.
steps: Make each service unable to start without touching the installed files: systemd drop-in with ExecStartPre=/bin/false; OpenRC rc_need="opfield-no-such-service" in /etc/conf.d/<unit>.
Re-run each installer.
Remove the drop-in or conf.d line and re-run.
expect: Each re-run exits 1, names the log source (journalctl -u <unit> or the OpenRC log) and prints its last lines; the output has no 'using manual mode'; no detached launcher runs.
After the cleanup each re-run is connected.

scenarios.title: Users that cannot run a daemon
preconditions: Snapshots of the file lists of /etc, /usr/local and /var/lib on the host.
steps: setup-monitoring-node.sh, setup-node.sh and setup-docker-node.sh with --user opfield-no-such-user and a fresh token.
setup-relay-node.sh with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=opfield-no-such-user.
setup-docker-node.sh --mode builder --user gwsvc; setup-storage-node.sh --user gwsvc.
expect: Every run exits 1 before any change; the relay prints the useradd hint; builder and storage say they run only as root.
The file lists are unchanged and the tokens are still unused.

scenarios.title: Monitoring: fresh root install, re-run, root to user and back, restart, reboot
preconditions: A host without monitoring-daemon.
steps: Run the monitoring setup command without --user.
Re-run it without a token.
Re-run with --user gwsvc; call sudo /usr/local/bin/monitoring-daemon version.
Re-run without --user.
Restart the service; reboot the host.
expect: Fresh: connected; service user root; /usr/local/bin/monitoring-daemon is a root binary; no host_identity_path in the config.
Re-run: connected, no new enrollment (certs unchanged), launcher directory kept.

To user: 'switching it to gwsvc'; connected; service user gwsvc; config, state and /usr/local/lib/monitoring-daemon owned by gwsvc; /usr/local/bin/monitoring-daemon is the root-owned wrapper and 'version' runs as gwsvc; host identity copy equals /var/lib/opfield/host-identity; same node id.

Back to root: 'ran as gwsvc; switching it to root'; connected; service user root; find over the three directories finds nothing owned by gwsvc; the wrapper is replaced by a root binary; host_identity_path removed.
Restart and reboot: online again within a minute, no restart loop in the service log.

scenarios.title: Monitoring: fresh non-root install, console, files, user to user
preconditions: A host without monitoring-daemon; gwsvc and gwsvc2 exist; another root daemon runs on the host.
steps: Run the monitoring setup command with --user gwsvc.
Open the node console and run id and touch /etc/opfield-test.
In Files: list, create, write and read in /var/lib/monitoring-daemon; create a file in /etc; read /var/lib/opfield/host-identity.
Re-run with --user gwsvc2.
expect: connected; service user gwsvc; host_identity_path points into /var/lib/monitoring-daemon and the copy equals the shared identity; Opfield shows one host for both daemons of the host.
Console: uid of gwsvc; touch fails with Permission denied.
Files: the state directory operations return 200; /etc and the root-only identity fail at once with permission denied, no hang.
User to user: the daemon is stopped, launcher/ is removed, everything belongs to gwsvc2, connected, same node id.

scenarios.title: nginx: fresh managed install as root, re-run, restart, reboot
preconditions: A host without nginx and nginx-daemon, reachable on 80/443 from the tool host.
steps: Run the nginx setup command with --nginx-mode managed.
Create a route on the node to a test upstream; request it over HTTPS with its name and with an unknown name.
Re-run without a token; restart nginx-daemon; reboot the host.
expect: Debian: nginx from the nginx.org stable repository; Alpine: the apk nginx package; version 1.25.1 or newer; connected; no 'Fresh enrollment token provided' line and no enrollment-backup directory.
The route answers 200; the unknown name gets a refused TLS handshake (ssl_reject_handshake).
Re-run connected without a new enrollment; after restart and reboot the node is online, the /run socket directories exist and the route answers 200.

scenarios.title: nginx: root to non-root and back
preconditions: An enrolled root nginx node with one route answering 200.
steps: Run nginx as its distribution user (www-data on Debian, nginx on Alpine) with CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE as docs/nodes.md describes (systemd drop-in; OpenRC: command_user and capabilities in /etc/conf.d/nginx), give it /etc/nginx, /var/log/nginx and the temp directories.
Re-run the installer with --user <that user> --nginx-mode integrate.
Create a second route, then reload by changing it.
Re-run without --user while nginx still runs as the user.
Run nginx as root again, re-run without --user.
expect: To user: connected; service user is the nginx user; the unit (systemd) or service (OpenRC) grants CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE; /etc/nginx, /var/www/acme-challenge, /etc/nginx-daemon, /var/lib/nginx-daemon and /run/nginx-daemon, /run/opfield-secure-links, /run/opfield-registry-links, /run/opfield-ingress-health belong to the user.
Route create and change apply (nginx -t binds 443) and both routes answer 200.
Without --user while nginx runs as the user: exit 1 'nginx runs as <user>, not root; nothing was changed'.
Back to root: connected; what the installer handed over belongs to root again; distribution files keep their owners; routes answer 200.

scenarios.title: nginx: fresh non-root install and user to user
preconditions: A host with Debian's nginx (1.25.1 or newer) prepared to run as www-data per docs/nodes.md, no nginx-daemon; a second user gwngx.
steps: Run the nginx setup command with --user www-data --nginx-mode integrate.
Create a route; check the node health.
Switch nginx to run as gwngx (drop-in User/Group, ownership), re-run with --user gwngx --nginx-mode integrate.
expect: connected; service user www-data; the route answers 200; node health configValid, ingressHealth.serving and configApplied are true.
User to user: connected as gwngx, everything the installer handed to www-data belongs to gwngx, the route answers 200.

scenarios.title: nginx: integrate with an existing configuration and --skip-nginx
preconditions: A host with Debian's nginx serving its own site with listen 443 ssl default_server and something on port 80.
steps: Run the nginx setup command with --nginx-mode integrate --skip-nginx as root.
Create a route; request the host's own site and the route.
expect: nginx is not reinstalled or upgraded; the host's site keeps answering; the daemon logs a warning that the node keeps its own 443 default server.
stub_status_url in /etc/nginx-daemon/config.yaml points at the local alternate port the installer chose, node stats report requests, the route answers 200.

scenarios.title: Docker: fresh root install with Docker Engine, watchdog and Secure Runtime preflight
preconditions: A host without Docker Engine and docker-daemon (Alpine: LXC with nesting and keyctl).
steps: Run the docker setup command with OPFIELD_LEASE_WATCHDOG_VERSION=<the watchdog release of <previous>>.
Run opfield-lease-watchdog status; deploy a container from the Opfield registry.
Re-run without a token and without OPFIELD_LEASE_WATCHDOG_VERSION; restart docker-daemon; reboot the host.
expect: Debian: docker-ce from download.docker.com; Alpine: the docker package; /etc/docker/daemon.json has json-file with max-size 50m and max-file 3; connected.

opfield-lease-watchdog runs as its own root service (systemd unit or OpenRC service) at the pinned release, its status shows a fresh heartbeat; the Secure Runtime preflight result is reported on the node (healthy, installable or unsupported) and does not fail the install.
The container runs; re-run connected without new enrollment and does not downgrade or replace the watchdog; after restart and reboot the node and the container are back.

scenarios.title: Docker: root to non-root and back with Secure Links and storage links
preconditions: A root docker node with a container behind a route on an nginx node (Secure Link) answering 200.
Debian: also a workload with a managed storage link that writes and reads objects every second.
steps: Re-run the installer with --user gwdock while probing the route and the storage link.
Deploy a blue/green deployment on the node; open the console.
Re-run without --user while probing.
expect: To user: gwdock is added to the docker group; connected; service user gwdock; the connector containers are recreated with GroupAdd of the daemon's gid; storage-relay.sock is gwdock:gwdock 0660; no *.previous-owner-* directory remains.
The route answers 200 and the storage link keeps working during and after the switch without a manual step; the deployment succeeds; the console shows gwdock with the docker group.
Back to root: connected; storage-relay.sock is 65532:65532 0600 with a fresh mtime; links and route work; Opfield still lists and manages the recreated storage connector.

scenarios.title: Docker: fresh non-root install, root-only features, user to user
preconditions: A host with Docker Engine and without docker-daemon; gwdock and gwdock2 exist.
steps: Run the docker setup command with --user gwdock.
Pull an image built by a Build Worker from the Opfield registry; deploy a container.
Open the volume create dialog (disk-image option), start a volume migration from and to the node, read container stats.
Re-run with --user gwdock2.
expect: connected; service user gwdock; /etc/docker/certs.d/127.0.0.1:5443 is owned by gwdock; the lease watchdog runs as a root service; the node advertises docker_daemon_non_root_v1.
The pull verifies TLS against the registry proxy and the container runs.
The disk-image option and volume migration name the non-root reason; stats report no log sizes as documented.
User to user: connected as gwdock2; the node is not listed under Availability excluded nodes.

scenarios.title: Docker: Secure Runtime on fresh, existing root and non-root nodes
preconditions: A VM docker node installed fresh by INS-DKR-01 where gVisor can run, and an LXC docker node running as gwdock without runsc.
steps: On the VM: docker-daemon runtime preflight runsc --json; create a Secure container.
Switch the VM node to --user gwdock; copy the one-line command from Node Details > Secure Runtime and run it; then sudo docker-daemon runtime install runsc.
On the LXC node: re-run the installer with --user gwdock --secure-runtime.
Try a Secure container with a bind mount, a GPU, a migration and a .gwca export.
expect: Preflight exits 0 healthy; the Secure container runs with runtime runsc.

The one-line command downloads and checks this release's installer, installs runsc from its own verified binary, Node Details shows healthy, the service user stays gwdock; 'runtime install' as the service user exits non-zero.
Where gVisor cannot run, --secure-runtime exits 1 with the preflight reason and leaves the daemon running as gwdock.
Bind mounts, GPU, migration and export are refused for the Secure workload.

scenarios.title: Relay: fresh root install, re-run, root to user and back, restart, reboot
preconditions: A host without a relay, its port 9443 reachable from the managed nodes.
steps: Create a relay node and run its command (port 9443).
Re-run without a token; re-run with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc; re-run without it.
Restart opfield-relay-supervisor; reboot the host.
Delete the relay node at the end.
expect: Fresh: the supervisor enrolls, the relay is ready in Settings > Relay, opfield-relay listens on 9443, a Secure Link route keeps answering after Rebalance.

Re-run without a token: exit 0 without enrollment errors, the same relay id and identity; re-running the original command with its used token exits 1 and says the relay keeps running with its previous identity.

To gwsvc: service user gwsvc, supervisor and worker run as gwsvc, no AmbientCapabilities for 9443; back to root: /usr/local/lib/opfield-relay/run-supervisor and all relay directories belong to root, find -user gwsvc is empty.
After restart and reboot the relay is ready again.

scenarios.title: Relay: fresh non-root install on a privileged port, group, setup log, user to user
preconditions: A host without a relay; gwsvc, gwsvc2 and a group gwrelay exist.
steps: Run the relay command with --service-port 853, OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc, OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_GROUP=gwrelay and OPFIELD_RELAY_SETUP_LOG=/root/relay-setup.log.
Re-run with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc2 and no group.
expect: Service user gwsvc, group gwrelay; the unit has AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE; the worker listens on 853 as gwsvc and the relay is ready with its advertised port 853 (managed nodes connect to it); /root/relay-setup.log holds the setup output.
User to user: everything belongs to gwsvc2 and its primary group; ready again; same relay id.

scenarios.title: Relay re-enrollment and refused tokens
preconditions: A remote relay of the pool.
steps: Stop the relay's supervisor until Settings > Relay shows it offline; click Re-enroll and run the command.
Run the same command again; run a command whose token belongs to another relay.
expect: Re-enrollment is ready with a new certificate; the pool keeps serving.
The used or foreign token exits 1 with the refused-token message; the relay keeps running with its current identity.

scenarios.title: A relay installed in protected mode
preconditions: A remote relay host with no relay installed, and a database on several servers that can use a relay witness.
steps: Install the relay with <setup command> --protected; on a second host, install with OPFIELD_RELAY_PROTECTED=1 and the plain <setup command>.
Re-run the installer without --protected; then run relay-supervisor protected status.

Turn witness hosting on for the relay in Settings > Relay; then run relay-supervisor protected on --allow-database-witness on the relay host, restart opfield-relay-supervisor and wait for its next report.
From Opfield, send the relay a command outside its own operation (for example a console or file request).
expect: Both relays are connected and /etc/opfield-relay/config.yaml has protected.enabled: true.
The re-run keeps protected mode on; status reports it on.
Before the local opt-in Settings > Relay shows the relay as needing the local opt-in and hosts no witness; after it, protected.allow_database_witness is true and the relay hosts the witness.
The relay refuses the command with an error that says the relay is protected; routing, drain, certificate renewal, logs and updates keep working.

scenarios.title: Build Worker: fresh install, egress profiles, re-run, restart, reboot
preconditions: A systemd host without docker-daemon, Git or iptables; a Git source whose build downloads npm packages and one that needs no network.
steps: Run the builder setup command (--mode builder, default egress).
Force a build of each source on this worker (move it to the top of the Nodes list).
Re-run with --builder-egress offline; build both again.
Re-run with --builder-egress internet; restart docker-daemon; reboot.
expect: Git and iptables are installed with apt; containerd, BuildKit, runc, CNI, Syft and Grype are downloaded and checksum-verified into /opt/opfield-builder/bin; opfield-builder-egress, opfield-builder-containerd and opfield-builder-buildkit units run; connected with every builder capability.
internet: both builds succeed; a build step reaching a private address, the worker host (its own addresses and the build bridge gateway) or the Opfield gRPC endpoint fails.
offline: the npm build fails at the download, the offline build succeeds.
After re-run, restart and reboot the worker takes builds again.

scenarios.title: Build Worker refused without systemd
preconditions: An OpenRC host; a fresh builder token.
steps: Run the builder setup command.
expect: Exit 1 with 'Builder nodes require systemd to supervise the isolated containerd and BuildKit services' before any download or enrollment; the token stays unused.

scenarios.title: Build Worker order
preconditions: Two online Build Workers in a node folder, a Git source.
steps: Force builds with each worker first in the folder.
Move one worker into a subfolder of that folder and force a build.
expect: The first online worker of the list order takes the build each time; a worker in a subfolder comes before the folder's own nodes.

scenarios.title: Storage: fresh install through the piped installer, disk selector, re-run, restart, reboot
preconditions: A VM without docker-daemon with a second mounted filesystem.
steps: Run curl … setup-storage-node.sh | sudo bash -s -- --opfield <opfield> --token <token> --opfield-cert-sha256 <cert> in a terminal without -y and pick the second filesystem in the disk selector.
Create a managed PostgreSQL and a SeaweedFS storage on the node; write data.
Re-run with -y --storage-root <the same path>; restart docker-daemon; reboot the VM.
expect: The installer downloads setup-database-node.sh from the same release and checks it, runs the loop and ext4 preflight, cleans up its probe, installs Docker, then enrolls; connected; storage root is the selected path; config has docker.mode storage.
The database and storage become ready with their images under the storage root.
Re-run keeps the storage root and enrollment; after restart and reboot the database and storage are ready with their data.

scenarios.title: Storage refused in an ordinary LXC guest
preconditions: An unprivileged LXC guest without loop devices and without docker-daemon.
steps: Run the storage setup command with -y.
expect: Exit 1 before enrollment with the LXC loop-device remediation; no image, loop attachment or mount is left; /etc/docker-daemon does not exist; the token stays unused.

scenarios.title: Legacy databases node updated to the candidate
preconditions: A VM without docker-daemon; Opfield runs <candidate>.
steps: Install with the <previous> installers: setup-daemon.sh --type databases --version <previous> … -y --storage-root <path>.
Create a managed Redis with data.
Update the node to <candidate> from its node page.
expect: The node shows as Storage; the Redis is ready.
After the update: same node id, enrollment and storage root; the node advertises the unified Storage capabilities (SeaweedFS can be created on it); the Redis data is intact.

scenarios.title: Ubuntu: packaged nginx 1.24 and a non-root nginx-daemon under AppArmor
preconditions: apt install nginx (1.24 from Ubuntu) running as root; fresh nginx tokens.
steps: Run the setup command with -y.
Run it with -y --skip-nginx.
Run it interactively and decline the upgrade; run it interactively and approve.
Prepare nginx (now from nginx.org) to run as www-data per docs/nodes.md, re-run with --user www-data --nginx-mode integrate, create and change a route.
expect: -y: exit 1 'nginx 1.25.1+ is required. Re-run interactively to approve the stable nginx upgrade.' before any config change or enrollment.
--skip-nginx: exit 1 '--skip-nginx requires nginx 1.25.1+; found 1.24…'.
Declined: stops before Opfield changes nginx config or enrolls; approved: nginx.org stable repository, nginx 1.25.1 or newer, connected.
Non-root under AppArmor: no AppArmor denial in the kernel log; nginx -t and reload succeed as www-data; routes answer 200.

scenarios.title: Ubuntu: distribution docker.io, AppArmor, Secure Runtime and resolved DNS
preconditions: apt install docker.io with a daemon.json of the operator's own; /etc/resolv.conf is the systemd-resolved stub; a route on an nginx node for Secure Link checks.
steps: Run the docker setup command as root with --secure-runtime.
Create a container; change its environment (recreate); run a container that resolves a public name and pulls from the Opfield registry.
Re-run with --user gwdock --secure-runtime; create a Default container behind a Secure Link route and, if Secure Runtime is healthy, a Secure container.
Read the kernel log for AppArmor denials.
expect: docker.io is kept (no docker-ce); the existing daemon.json keeps every key and value of the operator, --secure-runtime only adds runtimes.runsc after saving the original as daemon.json.opfield-backup, and a re-run changes neither file; connected.
--secure-runtime either installs runsc and Node Details shows Secure Runtime healthy, or exits 1 with the preflight reason and leaves the daemon running; it never reports success without runsc.
Recreate keeps the container's configuration; names resolve inside containers through the resolved upstream; the registry pull succeeds.
Non-root: connected as gwdock; connectors and workloads start with the docker-default profile; the route answers 200; no AppArmor denial for docker-daemon, its connectors or nginx.

scenarios.title: Ubuntu: Build Worker egress with systemd-resolved
preconditions: An Ubuntu guest without docker-daemon (reset after UBU-DOCKER) with the resolved stub; a Git source whose build downloads npm packages.
steps: Install a Build Worker with the default egress; force the build on it.
expect: The build resolves and downloads its dependencies and succeeds; the egress policy still blocks private ranges and the worker host itself.

scenarios.title: Ubuntu: non-root monitoring and relay under AppArmor
preconditions: The Ubuntu guest of UBU-DOCKER.
steps: Install monitoring with --user gwsvc and a relay with OPFIELD_RELAY_RUN_USER=gwsvc; open the console of the monitoring node; reboot.
expect: Both connected and back after the reboot; no AppArmor denials; the monitoring wrapper runs as gwsvc.

scenarios.title: Host console and file switches
preconditions: Enrolled nginx, docker, monitoring and relay nodes.
steps: Re-run each installer with --disable-console --disable-files; open the console and Files of each node and call execute_node_console_command over MCP.
Re-run each installer without the flags.
Set files.enabled: true only and restart; then set both true, set console.user: gwsvc2 on the nginx node (daemon as www-data) and on a root docker node, and restart both.
expect: Console: auth_error NODE_CONSOLE_DISABLED with the config hint; Files and the file API: 409 NODE_FILES_DISABLED; MCP returns NODE_CONSOLE_DISABLED; the node shows nodeConsoleDisabled/nodeFilesDisabled.
The re-run keeps both false.

Console off and files on shows the warning notice; with both on the console works. console.user on the nginx node: one startup error in the daemon log, the node page says console.user needs a root daemon, and the console and MCP return NODE_CONSOLE_USER_UNAVAILABLE; on the root docker node console sessions run as gwsvc2 in / (it has no home). Config ownership and mode are unchanged.

scenarios.title: Manual setup of nginx-daemon from the release files
preconditions: A host with Debian's nginx and no nginx-daemon; a fresh nginx token.
steps: Download nginx-daemon, checksums.txt and the .update.json manifest of <candidate>; verify the checksum; install the binary.
Write /etc/nginx-daemon/config.yaml with every key of the docs example, log_level debug and log_format text; run nginx-daemon install --opfield <opfield> --token <token> --opfield-cert-sha256 <cert>.
Write and start a systemd service; create a route with an access list using basic auth.
expect: Enrollment clears opfield.token in the file and writes the certificate paths under tls; the node is online.

The route config lands in nginx.config_dir, certificates in nginx.certs_dir, the htpasswd file in nginx.htpasswd_dir; ACME files go to nginx.acme_challenge_dir; logs in nginx.logs_dir stream in the UI; state lives in state_dir.
The daemon log is text at debug level.

scenarios.title: Docker service address
preconditions: A docker node with two addresses that hosts a managed database with a link, or published managed storage; a route to a container on the same node.
steps: Set the service address on the node page to the second address; read the database link (or published storage) endpoint and connect a client to it; read the route's rendered config; then clear the service address.
expect: The database link (or published storage) endpoint uses the configured address and the client connects through it; after clearing, it moves back to the first reported local address. The route's upstream stays its Secure Link socket and answers 200 either way.

scenarios.title: Daemons from the previous release update to the candidate
preconditions: Opfield runs <candidate>; nginx, docker, storage, builder and monitoring nodes run <previous>, among them a non-root monitoring node installed with --version <previous>.
A lease-mode Availability policy over two docker nodes.
steps: Install one more monitoring node with --version <previous> using the candidate installer.
Try to update an offline node, a relay node and a node already on <candidate>.
Select every node in Nodes > Update Nodes and update.
Apply an unchanged Compose revision on an updated docker node.
expect: The installer accepts the older daemon after 10 s of active service and warns that it does not report its Opfield connection.
The three updates are refused with their reasons.

Every node reports <candidate> and its capabilities; the two lease peers update one after another with waiting_for_lease_peers and the policy keeps its quorum; non-root daemons keep their user and /usr/local/lib/<daemon>/bin/<daemon>.previous exists.
The first apply recreates the Compose services once; the next one recreates nothing.

scenarios.title: Daemons on the candidate update themselves to a newer release
preconditions: <newer> is published on the preview channel and the update channel is preview; root and non-root daemons of each type run <candidate>.
steps: Update each node from Update Nodes; update the Relay Pool.
Restart each service afterwards.
expect: Each daemon verifies the signed manifest, replaces its binary atomically, passes the 30 s stability window and reports <newer>; non-root daemons replace /usr/local/lib/<daemon>/bin/<daemon> and keep the previous one, owner and service user unchanged; the wrapper is untouched.
Relays update supervisor first, then worker; after the restarts every node is online on <newer>.

scenarios.title: Relay Pool update from the previous release
preconditions: Remote relays on <previous>; Opfield on <candidate>.
Database link pools and storage links held open through the local relay, with probes that count dropped connections.
steps: Start Update Relay Pool.
In a second run abandon a step after the supervisor update and start again.
Start it once more with every relay already on the target.
Note what Settings > Relay shows for the local relay during its step.
expect: Each relay: supervisor self-update and reconnect first, then the worker update; the supervisor log has no listener with the old build version between 'starting self-update' and 'binary replaced successfully'; the run completes and relays leave drain.
The resumed run updates only the worker of the relay left after its supervisor update; a relay it finds already on the target is marked ready without draining.
Starting a run with every relay already on the target is refused with NO_UPDATE; no relay is drained or restarted.

With another ready relay that can serve the local relay's workloads and a local relay that already runs this release (in GET /api/system/relay the local instance's capabilities.features include drain_keeps_local_services_v1), the local relay's step drains it first (audit relay.instance.drain on the local instance, its workloads move, image pulls through the internal registry keep working during the drain, the drain waits as for a remote relay and Force disconnect works on it), then recreates, verifies and resumes it (relay.instance.resume); held connections move instead of dropping, a pull cut by the recreate is retried by the Docker daemon, and abandon is refused with 409 RELAY_UPDATE_COMMITTED only once the recreate began. Without such a relay, or on the update from a local relay older than this release, the local relay is recreated at once, connections drop once and reconnect, and relay_pool_update_steps.error of the local step names why.

scenarios.title: Launchers update themselves; an older launcher process gets one service restart
preconditions: <newer> is published on the preview channel and the update channel is preview.
Docker and nginx nodes, root and non-root (--user gwsvc), run <previous>, and their launcher processes started on <previous> or earlier: no service restart since.
On those nodes database link pools, a storage link and a Route Secure Link WebSocket stay open, with probes that count dropped and refused connections.
steps: Update every node to <candidate>; wait until launcher/launcher-refresh.json on each node shows phase trial.
Update every node to <newer>; once the node is online, note the launcher PID (launcher/owner.json) and the daemon PID (launcher/child.json).
Wait 2 minutes and note both PIDs again.
Update the nodes once more, to a build of <newer> with another version, and wait 2 minutes.
expect: The update to <candidate> restarts the daemon under its launcher, as before; the node details show the launcher version Unknown.

The update to <newer> restarts the whole service once: under systemd as root at once, as gwsvc after RestartSec, under OpenRC after respawn_delay; the update result (Opfield log: Daemon update staged) and the daemon log say so; the probes count one cut, as for any update. The node comes back on <newer> with the capabilities launcher_listener_keep_v1, launcher_self_update_v1 and launcher_openrc_v1.

Within 2 minutes after the <newer> daemon connected, the launcher execs into the launcher of <newer>: launcher and daemon PIDs unchanged, /proc/<launcher pid>/exe names <launcher>.next and launcher-refresh.json shows attempts 1, no probe counts a drop or a refused connection, the daemon reconnects its control session once and the node details show the launcher version <newer>.

The last update restarts only the daemon under the launcher (launcher PID unchanged, no service restart in the journal or the OpenRC log); that daemon confirms the launcher (the launcher copy replaced, launcher-refresh.json gone until the new daemon stages itself), then the launcher updates itself in place again.

scenarios.title: Relay Pool operations
preconditions: Two remote relays and Secure Link routes and database links under load.
steps: Rebalance; drain a relay with an open database link pool, then Force disconnect; Renew certificate on a relay.
Stop the supervisor of a remote relay whose policy has not expired and try to remove it.
expect: Assignments move after successful probes without failed requests; drain waits, Force disconnect is audited; the renewed certificate is served without dropping connections.

Removal is refused with 409 RELAY_OFFLINE_REMOVAL_UNSAFE whose details.removableAfter is the later of the relay's policy expiry and 90 s after it was last seen; Settings > Relay shows 'Can be removed after <local date and time>' for it with Remove disabled, and GET /api/system/relay reports the same removableAfter.

scenarios.title: Route maintenance without reloads
preconditions: An nginx node with several routes under 10 rps keep-alive probes; reload counter from the nginx error log.
steps: Toggle maintenance 5 times through UI, API and MCP; redeem a team access code.
Restart nginx-daemon and reboot the node while one route is in maintenance.
Toggle on a route with secure_link in its advanced config.
expect: 0 reloads and 0 errors on the neighbours; 503 in maintenance and 200 with the access cookie; the upstream never sees the access cookie.
The route stays in maintenance after restart and reboot.
The secure_link route enters maintenance without a duplicate-directive error.

scenarios.title: Ingress groups with two members
preconditions: Two nginx nodes on the candidate.
steps: Create a group with both nodes, move a domain and its routes onto it.
Stop one member's nginx-daemon, toggle maintenance and change a route, start it again.
Remove a member.
expect: Both members serve every route and their health endpoints answer 200.
The offline member gets the flag and the change after reconnect within a minute.
The removed member drains and its configs are cleaned up.

scenarios.title: ACME, Pages, logs and health on a non-root nginx node
preconditions: A non-root nginx node.
steps: Place an HTTP-01 challenge file; deploy a Pages project; open the route log stream; read node health.
expect: nginx serves the challenge file written by the daemon user; Pages answers over HTTPS; log lines stream for each request; configValid, ingressHealth.serving and configApplied are true.

scenarios.title: Container stop, restart, kill and delete
preconditions: A docker node; containers that exit on SIGTERM and that ignore it; docker events logged.
steps: Stop, restart, kill (SIGKILL, SIGHUP) and delete through REST, MCP and UI, including delete right after stop with timeout 120.
Stop through an nginx route with a 60 s read timeout.
expect: Fast containers answer 200 after die; slow ones 202 with a task after about 45 s and finish; no 409; no 504 through the proxy; the UI shows stopping and then exited without a reload and lets Remove queue the deletion.

scenarios.title: Migrations between docker nodes, including an old engine
preconditions: Two docker nodes on a current engine and one on Docker 20.10; deployments with routes.
steps: Migrate a deployment between the current nodes in both directions; migrate a container from the 20.10 node; save an env variable without recreate and run the preflight.
expect: 0 reloads on the ingress, 503 from the first request after entering until cutover, no 502; the 20.10 migration completes; MIGRATION_ENV_PENDING names the key.

scenarios.title: Compose, archives and log limits
preconditions: A docker node whose Docker Engine the installer installed and one with its own daemon.json log-opts.
steps: Apply a Compose revision changing one service; Pull & Apply.
Export a container as portable and as registry-backed .gwca and import both on another node.
Create a container on each node; inspect its LogConfig.
expect: Only the changed service is recreated.
Both imports run with the same configuration and empty volumes.
json-file 50m × 3 on the installer node; the other node keeps the host's options.

scenarios.title: GPU workloads
preconditions: A docker node with a GPU and its driver and runtime installed by the operator.
steps: Attach the GPU to a container and to a deployment; try to migrate and export them.
expect: The device is attachable, the workload sees it, GPU metrics report; migration and export are refused.

scenarios.title: Availability, Replicated mode
preconditions: Two docker nodes and an nginx node; a container with a route; reload counter.
steps: Enable Replicated with two placements; Stop; Start; update the container env (rollout); Disable.
expect: Reloads: enable 2, stop and drain 1 per member, disable 1; no 502 while another copy serves; the rollout completes even for an app that ignores SIGTERM; neighbours see no resets beyond those reloads.

scenarios.title: Availability failover in lease mode
preconditions: Two docker nodes (one non-root) with lease watchdogs, two remote relays, all on the candidate for 2 minutes; a disposable node can be powered off.
steps: Enable Failover with priority order; wait for lease mode.
Power off the holder; later power it on (failback after the delay).
Stop the Opfield app and power off the new holder; start Opfield again.
Stop the lease watchdog on one candidate.
expect: The policy enters lease mode with participants settled.
The next candidate serves within 45 s; failback runs after failbackDelaySeconds.
Failover happens without Opfield; Opfield records docker.availability.lease_failover after it returns.
The candidate is listed under excluded nodes with watchdog_missing.

scenarios.title: Managed databases and object storage
preconditions: A Storage node with free loop devices; docker events logged.
steps: Create PostgreSQL and Redis with publishTcp true and no port; toggle publication; ClickHouse with both native ports.
docker stop, docker kill and kill -9 of the engine processes of SeaweedFS, Redis and PostgreSQL.
Exhaust loop devices to fail a create, free them and retry; move a record file aside on a live database and storage and retry.
expect: One create and one start per engine; the port Opfield shows is the one the container listens on.
A requested stop stays ready; a real crash shows stopped 'keeps stopping' on the next pass.
Retry provisions ready with takesOverExistingData as documented; data and objects survive.

scenarios.title: Backups, restores and copy jobs
preconditions: Managed PostgreSQL, Redis and ClickHouse with data; an S3 destination.
steps: Run a manual backup of each; restore each into a new database; run a copy job between two S3 storages with dryRun and then copy.
expect: Backups succeed and restores contain the data; the copy job copies the buckets and reports the check result.

scenarios.title: Opfield fresh install, dry run and re-run as update
preconditions: A clean host with Docker Engine and Compose v2, curl and openssl.
steps: curl … install.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run.
curl … install.sh | OPFIELD_INSTALL_LOG_FILE=/root/gw-install.log bash -s -- --https.
Complete the wizard with the printed setup code.
Run install.sh again.
expect: The dry run verifies the signed release, prints the plan and creates no file in /opt/opfield.
The install prints the URL, the System CA fingerprint and the setup code; https on :3000; /root/gw-install.log is 0600 and holds the run.
The wizard completes and the setup code stops working.
The re-run updates without prompts, keeps .env secrets and the relay container when its digest is unchanged.

scenarios.title: Opfield install variants
preconditions: The host of GW-01 after removing that installation (docker compose down -v in /opt/opfield).
steps: Interactive install in a terminal: choose HTTP in the transport prompt.
Remove it; OPFIELD_INSTALL_DIR=/srv/gw-a OPFIELD_WEB_TRANSPORT=http install.sh; interrupt it after the images are pulled; run it again.
Remove it; write a daemon.json with log-opts to /root/daemon-test.json and run install.sh --install-dir /srv/gw-b --http with OPFIELD_DOCKER_DAEMON_CONFIG=/root/daemon-test.json.
Switch internal HTTPS on and off in Settings > General.
expect: HTTP on :3000 after choosing HTTP.
The second run says 'fresh install (resumed)', keeps DB_PASSWORD and PKI_MASTER_KEY of the first and prints a setup code.
The install lives in /srv/gw-b and its docker-compose.yml has no logging sections; without the variable the sections are present.
Opfield restarts on the selected transport each time.

scenarios.title: Opfield built from a source checkout
preconditions: A clean host with a checkout of the candidate.
steps: install.sh --source-dir <checkout> --image opfield-local --https.
Run install.sh --source-dir <checkout> again on the installed host.
Remove it; OPFIELD_SOURCE_DIR=<checkout> OPFIELD_IMAGE=opfield-local2 install.sh.
expect: Images opfield-local:local-<time> and opfield-local/relay:local-<time> are built; OPFIELD_RELAY_MANAGED=false in .env; setup completes.
The second run stops with '--source-dir is supported only for a fresh Opfield installation'.
The environment form builds opfield-local2 the same way.

scenarios.title: Release upgrade end-to-end from the 2.10 line
preconditions: A clean disposable host with Internet access.
steps: scripts/release-upgrade-e2e.sh --candidate <candidate> --logs-out <file>.
expect: Every check prints PASS (install of the base, update with bounded API downtime, daemon and relay updates with the lease watchdog installed, the base updater's rollback, fresh candidate install); exit 0.

scenarios.title: In-app Opfield update and offline behaviour
preconditions: The stand Opfield on <previous> with nodes, routes, a status page and database links.
steps: Start a migration, then Check for updates and update to <candidate>; watch the wait list; press Update now on a second try.
Switch the update channel to preview and back to stable.
Stop the app container for 5 minutes, then start it.
expect: The update waits for the migration, refuses new operations meanwhile, snapshots the database and deletes the dump after success; nodes reconnect; app-only update keeps database link streams.
Release-candidate offers appear only on preview.
While stopped, routes and the status page are served from nginx, containers run, links of ready bindings keep working; daemons reconnect after start.

scenarios.title: Opfield restored on a new host from a configuration export
preconditions: A Opfield of <candidate> with nodes, a paid licence and a configuration export downloaded from Settings.
A clean second host with Docker Engine and Compose v2, curl and openssl.
steps: On the second host: install.sh --restore <export file> --public-url https://<new host>:3000 --grpc-target <new host>:9443.
Run it once more without --public-url and --grpc-target in a terminal.
Stop the old Opfield.
expect: The installer installs the release that made the export, restores it without prompts and prints the sign-in link; the licence is not carried over and a cloud enrollment is dropped.
Without the options it asks for the address and keeps the answers.
The nodes of the old Opfield move to the new address by themselves and show online.

scenarios.title: Opfield console on its own domain with a Let's Encrypt certificate
preconditions: A clean host reachable from the internet on ports 80 and 443, with a DNS name pointing to it.
steps: install.sh --domain <name> --acme-email <email>.
install.sh --domain <name> without --acme-email, and install.sh --acme-email <email> alone.
Open http://<name>/ and https://<name>/.
expect: The console answers on https://<name>/ on port 443 with a Let's Encrypt certificate that renews by itself; the public URL is https://<name>.
Both runs stop with the message that --domain needs --acme-email and that --acme-email is used with --domain.
http redirects to https; no port appears in the URL.

scenarios.title: Hosting: adoption and node creation on Proxmox
preconditions: A Proxmox hosting connector with an API token; a guest whose node runs a non-root daemon.
steps: Sync the connector; create a hosted monitoring node; fail its installation once and use Retry installation.
expect: The existing guest is adopted by host identity without a manual match; the hosted node becomes ready only after its daemon connects; retry keeps the VM and node id and rotates the token.

scenarios.title: Dashboard attention dot
preconditions: An admin and a folder-limited user.
steps: Produce an expired PKI certificate, a stopped pinned container, a flapping pinned node, and a failed TLS replica outside the limited user's scope.
expect: The dot and a matching Dashboard warning appear and clear together; the limited user sees neither for the out-of-scope replica.

scenarios.title: Secure-link network address pool
preconditions: An enrolled docker node on the release under test and a running target container with a TCP port.
steps: Create a container link to the target from a container on the node and read the link network's subnet with docker network inspect.
Set docker.secure_links.subnet_pool to a different /20 in /etc/docker-daemon/config.yaml, restart docker-daemon, and create a second container link.
Remove the setting, restart, and create a third link; delete all three links.
expect: The first network is a /26 inside the default pool that docs/nodes.md names, and the connector holds its base address +2.
The second network is a /26 inside the configured /20; the first link keeps working.
The third network is again inside the default pool; deleting the links removes their networks.
